transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling Card Member Services. My name is Marcus. How can I help you today?
Customer: Hi Marcus, I'm calling because I have a problem with a purchase that showed up on my latest statement.
Agent: I can certainly look into that for you. May I have your full name and your billing zip code to get started?
Customer: Yes, it's Dana Whitcombe, and my zip code is 97201.
Agent: Thank you, Dana. Which statement is this charge appearing on, and who is the merchant?
Customer: It's on my statement dated October 03, 2026, and the merchant listed is Larkspur Home Goods.
Agent: Got it, Larkspur Home Goods. And what is the dollar amount and transaction date for that item?
Customer: It was charged on September 23, 2026, and the total was $89.00.
Agent: Thank you. Can you tell me a bit more about what you purchased and what happened?
Customer: Sure. I bought a ceramic table lamp from their website. But when the package arrived, I opened it up and the lamp was completely shattered inside the box.
Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. Were you able to use the lamp in any way?
Customer: No, definitely not. It was literally broken into dozens of sharp pieces, so I never got to use it at all.
Agent: Did you reach out to Larkspur Home Goods about the delivery?
Customer: I sent them an email with pictures the day it arrived, but I haven't gotten any response back from them yet.
Agent: Alright. So just to make sure I have all the details noted correctly, you bought a ceramic table lamp online from Larkspur Home Goods for $89.00 on September 23rd, it arrived broken in pieces so you were never able to use it, and you've tried emailing them about the issue from your October 03, 2026 statement without a reply.
Customer: Yes, that is exactly what happened.
